task.title: Review DevOps configuration sources
task.shortdesc: Identify the current BPM configuration sources, record effective runtime values, and separate ordinary settings from unsupported secret-management expectations.

prereq.p: BPM is deployed from source on Linux or through WSL, and the administrator can inspect the shell environment, optional .env file, and source checkout.

context.p: BPM loads settings from environment variables with the BPM_ prefix and from a repository-root .env file. BPM does not provide an application-managed secret store, credential vault, API token setting, encryption-key setting, or production configuration profile.

step.cmd: List the configuration sources used for this run.

info.p: Record whether values come from shell exports, a local .env, or the documented defaults. Keep .env local to the checkout and do not commit it.

step.cmd: Record the runtime settings that affect process behavior.

info.p: Include BPM_APP_NAME, BPM_APP_VERSION, BPM_DEBUG, BPM_HOST, BPM_PORT, BPM_RELOAD, BPM_API_PREFIX, BPM_DEFAULT_LOCALE, BPM_SUPPORTED_LOCALES, BPM_I18N_DIR, and BPM_DOCUMENTATION_SITE_DIR. Defaults are local-source defaults, not production policy.

step.cmd: Record data, schema, and network-related settings separately.

info.p: Track BPM_DATABASE_URL, BPM_DB_ECHO, BPM_ENABLE_CORS, BPM_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS, BPM_SCHEMA_BASE_URL, BPM_SCHEMA_CACHE_DIR, and BPM_SCHEMA_HTTP_TIMEOUT. Treat database URLs and network origins as operational evidence even when they contain no password.

step.cmd: Keep secrets out of BPM configuration examples.

info.note: BPM source deployment documentation does not provide authentication setup, managed secrets, encryption-at-rest configuration, token rotation, tenant isolation, or secret redaction guarantees. If your environment needs those controls, record them as external platform controls rather than BPM-supported features.

result.p: The deployment has a reviewed configuration inventory that matches current source settings and does not imply unsupported secret-management behavior.

postreq.p: Use the storage, network, and operational-boundary topics to review the impact of the recorded values before exposing BPM beyond a controlled local environment.
